pure-announcement.rationale: It is mechanism-centric documentation, and its framing — SBOMs say what shipped, EDR says what ran, responders also need on-disk developer-endpoint state — transfers beyond the Bumblebee tool itself.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept touches developer-endpoint inventory or supply-chain exposure response; OSV format is about advisory interchange, not scanning endpoints against advisories.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The scanner's claimed behavior (read-only sources, record schemas, selftest) is verifiable directly from the open Apache-2.0 repo it links.

durability.rationale: The gap analysis and read-only-inventory pattern will hold, but the durable value rides on a days-old v0.1 single-vendor tool, and much of the note is a coverage matrix, flag list, and pinned versions (Go 1.25+, schema 0.2.0, 'not parsed in v0.1') that will churn.

actionability.rationale: It changes how a responder would handle the next package compromise — check developer machines' lockfile, extension, and MCP-config state via read-only metadata against an advisory catalog — an action that stands even without adopting Bumblebee specifically.

atomicity.rationale: Every section serves one idea, read-only endpoint inventory matched against exposure catalogs, which states cleanly in a single paragraph.
